BLS employment.body: <?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?><feed xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom"><id>bls.gov:feed:empsit</id><title>Employment Situation</title><subtitle>"The Employment Situation (EMPSIT) release contains data from two surveys. The Current Employment Statistics program surveys businesses on a monthly basis and provides data by industry on employment, hours, and earnings of workers on nonfarm payrolls. The Current Population Survey is a monthly survey of households; it provides data on the labor force, employment, unemployment, and persons not in the labor force. Issued monthly. For more information, see www.bls.gov/cps/ and www.bls.gov/ces/. "</subtitle><updated>2026-11-06T07:50:31.965-05:00</updated><logo>https://www.bls.gov/images/bls_emblem_lrg.gif</logo><icon>https://www.bls.gov/favicon.ico</icon><author><name>Bureau of Labor Statistics Publications</name><uri>https://www.bls.gov</uri></author><rights>US Bureau of Labor Statistics</rights><entry><title>Payroll employment rises by 165,000 in October; unemployment rate changes little at 4.1%</title><link href="https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_11062026.htm"/><id>empsit-2026_11_06__07_50_31</id><content>Total nonfarm payroll employment rose by 165,000 in October, and the unemployment rate changed little at 4.1 percent. Employment increased in professional and business services, in health care, and in transportation and warehousing.</content><published>2026-11-06T07:50:31.965-05:00</published><updated>2026-11-06T07:50:31.965-05:00</updated><category>News Release</category></entry><entry><title>Both payroll employment (+29,000) and unemployment rate (4.2%) change little in September</title><link href="https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_10022026.htm"/><id>empsit-2026_10_02__07_51_08</id><content>Both nonfarm payroll employment (+29,000) and the unemployment rate  (4.2 percent) changed little in September. Employment in all major  industries changed little over the month.</content><published>2026-10-02T07:51:08.289-04:00</published><updated>2026-10-02T07:51:08.289-04:00</updated><category>News Release</category></entry><entry><title>Payroll employment increases by 162,000 in August; unemployment rate unchanged at 4.1%</title><link href="https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_09042026.htm"/><id>empsit-2026_09_04__07_51_08</id><content>Total nonfarm payroll employment increased by 162,000 in August,  and the unemployment rate was unchanged at 4.1 percent. Employment  increased in food services and drinking places and in local  government education. The information industry lost jobs.</content><published>2026-09-04T07:51:08.695-04:00</published><updated>2026-09-04T07:51:08.695-04:00</updated><category>News Release</category></entry><entry><title>Both payroll employment (-23,000) and unemployment rate (4.1%) change little in July</title><link href="https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_08072026.htm"/><id>empsit-2026_08_07__07_50_34</id><content>Both nonfarm payroll employment (-23,000) and the unemployment rate (4.1 percent) changed little in July. Employment declined in local government education and retail trade. Employment continued to trend up in health care.</content><published>2026-08-07T07:50:34.021-04:00</published><updated>2026-08-07T07:50:34.021-04:00</updated><category>News Release</category></entry><entry><title>Both payroll employment (+57,000) and unemployment rate (4.2%) change little in June</title><link href="https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_07022026.htm"/><id>empsit-2026_07_02__07_50_52</id><content>Both total nonfarm payroll employment (+57,000) and the unemployment rate (4.2 percent) changed little in June. Employment continued to trend up in professional and business services, social assistance, and health care. Leisure and hospitality lost jobs.</content><published>2026-07-02T07:50:52.662-04:00</published><updated>2026-07-02T07:50:52.662-04:00</updated><category>News Release</category></entry><entry><title>Payroll employment increases by 172,000 in May; unemployment rate unchanged at 4.3%</title><link href="https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_06052026.htm"/><id>empsit-2026_06_05__08_30_00</id><content>Total nonfarm payroll employment increased by 172,000 in May, and the unemployment rate was unchanged at 4.3 percent. Job gains occurred in leisure and hospitality, local government, and health care. Employment in financial activities declined.</content><published>2026-06-05T08:30:00-04:00</published><updated>2026-06-05T08:30:00-04:00</updated><category>News Release</category></entry><entry><title>Payroll employment edges up by 115,000 in April; unemployment rate unchanged at 4.3%</title><link href="https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_05082026.htm"/><id>empsit-2026_05_08__08_30_00</id><content>Total nonfarm payroll employment edged up by 115,000 in April, and the unemployment rate was unchanged at 4.3 percent. Job gains occurred in health care, transportation and warehousing, and retail trade. Federal government employment continued to decline.</content><published>2026-05-08T08:30:00-04:00</published><updated>2026-05-08T08:30:00-04:00</updated><category>News Release</category></entry><entry><title>Payroll employment increases by 178,000 in March; unemployment rate changes little at 4.3%</title><link href="https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_04032026.htm"/><id>empsit-2026_04_03__08_30_00</id><content>Total nonfarm payroll employment increased by 178,000 in March, and the unemployment rate changed little at 4.3 percent. Job gains occurred in health care, in construction, and in transportation and warehousing. Federal government employment continued to decline.</content><published>2026-04-03T08:30:00-04:00</published><updated>2026-04-03T08:30:00-04:00</updated><category>News Release</category></entry><entry><title>Payroll employment edges down 92,000 in February; unemployment rate changes little at 4.4%</title><link href="https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_03062026.htm"/><id>empsit-2026_03_06__08_30_00</id><content>Total nonfarm payroll employment edged down by 92,000 in February, and the unemployment rate changed little at 4.4 percent. Employment in health care decreased, reflecting strike activity. Retail trade lost jobs.</content><published>2026-01-09T08:30:00-05:00</published><updated>2026-01-09T08:30:00-05:00</updated><category>News Release</category></entry><entry><title>Both payroll employment (+64,000) and unemployment rate (4.6%) change little in November</title><link href="https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_12162025.htm"/><id>empsit-2025_12_16__08_30_00</id><content>Total nonfarm payroll employment changed little in November (+64,000) and has changed little since April. BLS CPI.body: <?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?><feed xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom"><id>bls.gov:feed:cpi</id><title>Consumer Price Index</title><subtitle>"The Consumer Price Index (CPI) is a measure of the average change over time in the prices paid by urban consumers for a fixed market basket of goods and services. The CPI is based on the prices of food, clothing, shelter, fuel, drugs, transportation fares, doctors' and dentists' fees, and other goods and services that people buy for day-to-day living. This release is issued monthly. For more information, visit the Consumer Price Indexes home page at www.bls.gov/cpi/. "</subtitle><updated>2026-10-14T07:50:31.2-04:00</updated><logo>https://www.bls.gov/images/bls_emblem_lrg.gif</logo><icon>https://www.bls.gov/favicon.ico</icon><author><name>Bureau of Labor Statistics Publications</name><uri>https://www.bls.gov</uri></author><rights>US Bureau of Labor Statistics</rights><entry><title>CPI for all items increases 0.6% in September; gasoline rises</title><link href="https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/cpi_10142026.htm"/><id>cpi-2026_10_14__07_50_31</id><content>In September, the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers rose 0.6 percent, seasonally  adjusted (SA), and rose 3.7 percent over the year, not seasonally adjusted (NSA). BLS PPI.body: <?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?><feed xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom"><id>bls.gov:feed:ppi</id><title>Producer Price Index</title><subtitle>"The Producer Price Indexes (PPI) news release presents measures of average price change over time in the selling prices received by domestic producers of goods and services.  The output of all industries in the goods-producing sector of the economy¿agriculture, forestry, fishing, mining, and manufacturing¿are included in the PPI. Service sector coverage is expanding.  This release is issued monthly. For more information, visit the Producer Price Indexes home page at www.bls.gov/ppi/. "</subtitle><updated>2026-10-15T07:50:51.146-04:00</updated><logo>https://www.bls.gov/images/bls_emblem_lrg.gif</logo><icon>https://www.bls.gov/favicon.ico</icon><author><name>Bureau of Labor Statistics Publications</name><uri>https://www.bls.gov</uri></author><rights>US Bureau of Labor Statistics</rights><entry><title>PPI for final demand increases 1.3% in September; goods advance 2.6%, services rise 0.8%</title><link href="https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/ppi_10152026.htm"/><id>ppi-2026_10_15__07_50_51</id><content>The Producer Price Index for final demand increased 1.3 percent in September. Prices for final  demand goods rose 2.6 percent, and the index for final demand services advanced 0.8 percent.  Prices for final demand moved up 6.3 percent for the 12 months ended in September.</content><published>2026-10-15T07:50:51.146-04:00</published><updated>2026-10-15T07:50:51.146-04:00</updated><category>News Release</category></entry><entry><title>PPI for final demand moves up 0.4% in August; goods advance 1.1%, services rise 0.1%</title><link href="https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/ppi_09102026.htm"/><id>ppi-2026_09_10__07_50_35</id><content>The Producer Price Index for final demand moved up 0.4 percent in August. Prices for final  demand goods advanced 1.1 percent, and the index for final demand services increased 0.1  percent.
